rulings.reason: the live half of P2-03/BL-16: exactly ONE Host boot; if it fails, stop and report, no retry without authorisation

RETRY AUTHORISED, funded by ONE of the remaining two P2-04 starts. The first attempt's abort was an INSTRUMENT defect (rows emitted, never given to the World), not a product finding, and that class is now guarded by a check plus a mutation control that requires it to go RED. Spending a second start on a genuinely new guard is not the same as retrying the same hope.
conditions: go-no-go itself must evaluate the rows-given-to-the-World handoff, not only the dry run
the pre-boot assertion is content-bearing: the rows the World composes equal the emitted rows by identity, in order, with the health probe row present (a length check would have passed last time)
stage attribution must distinguish composition vs member-install vs delegate-dispatch, so an abort teaches WHICH handoff is broken
if this attempt aborts before any row is judged: stop and report; do NOT ask for a third start

note: The driver and go-no-go both read this file: a start is allowed only while the shared ledger's boot rows for this lane are fewer than `authorisedStarts`. A third boot requires a NEW ruling appended here — editing `authorisedStarts` upward without a ruling entry is a self-authorisation and is called out in the README.
